notes: Checked official county home, Planning & Zoning, and Economic Development pages plus targeted searches for data center/server farm/colocation/hyperscale. No county-level data center project, permit, rezoning, tax abatement, or local news lead found; search results were dominated by non-project references and social discussion.

Official sources show active county attention to data centers: commissioners approved Resolution 952-26 on July 2, 2026 adopting an emergency moratorium on issuance of permits for data center development in unincorporated Elmore County. The county water-supply study discusses data centers as a potential new industry and cites Meta's Kuna project as an example, but I found no named Elmore County project/application/developer. A LinkedIn listing marketed 160 acres near Simco Road for data center use, treated as a site-marketing lead rather than a confirmed project.

Checked Franklin County, Idaho official site, Planning & Zoning, agendas/minutes, and targeted data-center searches. No Idaho project found. Search hits for Franklin County data center proposals/rules were for other states, especially Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Missouri.

Checked official Planning & Building, Comprehensive Plan, and P&Z minutes. Minutes with data-center mentions were for solar/power-generation discussion and described broader regional demand/chatter, including a data center near Idaho Falls 'not necessarily here'; no Fremont County data center project/application found.

notes: This appears to be a county internal IT/server/broadband facility, not a commercial data center development. Included as a low-scale official data-center reference so the county is not falsely treated as having no data-center activity.

Targeted official/news searches found no commercial or development data center project. The main official hit was a 2019 county IT/server upgrade proposal mentioning a data center in the context of county computing infrastructure, and hazard-plan references to NOAA/National Climatic Data Center, neither indicating a data center development project.

Checked official county home, Planning/Zoning/Building, ordinance page, and searches for Rigby/Roberts/Jefferson County data center/server farm/hyperscale. No county-level project found. Official records found data-center references only in policy context: a 2026 legislative update discussed state bills on data-center water use/electric accounts, and 2023 urban-renewal minutes discussed HB 359 limits for large data centers applying for sales-tax exemption. No named Jerome County project, permit, or rezoning found.

project_name: Unnamed large data center over northern Rathdrum Prairie Aquifer
aliases: Data Center Inquiry Over the Aquifer
status_detail: Kootenai County Rathdrum Prairie Aquifer Protection District minutes say county Community Development staff advised there was an inquiry for a large data center over the northern extent of the aquifer, that it would require rezoning, and that an application had been submitted. County later adopted a data-center building-permit moratorium and codified strict CUP standards barring data centers over the Rathdrum Prairie Aquifer.
notes: Most concrete commercial project lead in this batch, but the official minutes do not name the applicant/developer, site address, city, or capacity. Status set to planned because an application was reportedly submitted; later moratorium/ordinance may make approval difficult or impossible.
